brief: The canvas displays the surface of aged, yellowed newsprint, covered in dense layers of textual failure. Overlapping fields of wet, dark ink creep across the paper, forming redundant marginalia and cross-outs. The viewer observes the delicate interaction between the deep, faded blue-black ink and the fibrous, creamy yellow texture of the paper. There is no required input; the piece is a study of forgotten information and structural decay, where time itself is the primary mechanism of change.

statement: This sketch presents a contemplative study of decay and forgotten information. It depicts the surface of aged newsprint with a creamy yellow texture, overlaid with layers of wet ink that creep and fade across the paper. The piece explores how time transforms materials—how the deep blue-black ink interacts with the fibrous paper, creating redundant marginalia and cross-outs. The static nature of the composition reflects on how forgotten information persists, slowly eroded by time. Through subtle motion and layered visual effects, it captures a quiet meditation on structural decay and the passage of memory.
